touches.text: Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
Transient: the transient tree (what the logging tree becomes).

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there. Trouble tickets are logging items.
Cairn's own sleep has a lot to do, including clearing the logging tree of things older than 30 days.
Every device has a shim. Each shim is its own process, one per instance, and connects to the bus as a client (agreed 2026-10-26).
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.
Processes all messages from the bus for its device.
Trouble tickets (3.3.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.2.8.1.3).
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). USERS: everyone who writes a record.
question: the open-question door: a decision only you can make, bound to its ticket, answered in your words. → Ticket (3.3.5)? Operator?

conflicts.text: It answers what it can itself; when it can't (eg a health question it holds no answer to), it wakes the device and asks.
conflicts.ticket_says: BaseShim's default receive() drops (disposes of) an origin:test envelope after recording it to test_debris.jsonl, unless the device's shim declares handles_test_mail=True. The shim silently discards the message without delivering it to its device or bouncing it back.
conflicts.why: The outline prescribes that a shim 'answers what it can itself; when it can't…it wakes the device and asks.' Disposal is neither: the ticket adds a third mode where the shim receives a message and discards it without interaction with its device. This contradicts the binary presented in the outline (answer-or-escalate). Note: decision 21 in the ticket supersedes this with a different approach (returning unacted-on traffic), but the ticket as written describes disposal, which conflicts with 5.7.3.2.3.
